subject: Biology

nodes.text: respiration releases the energy stored in food so cells can use it
glucose is the main fuel that is broken down during respiration
in aerobic respiration oxygen is used to break glucose down completely
the released energy is stored in ATP, the molecule cells spend to do work
aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water as waste products
without enough oxygen, anaerobic respiration releases much less energy and produces lactic acid or alcohol
most respiration takes place in the mitochondria of the cell

textbookPhrasings: Cellular respiration is the process by which cells break down glucose in the presence of oxygen to release energy in the form of ATP.
Respiration is the process of releasing energy from food by oxidising glucose to form carbon dioxide and water.
The mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell because respiration occurs there.
referenceFacts: Oxygen is used in aerobic respiration
Carbon dioxide is produced as a waste product
Energy is stored in ATP molecules
Anaerobic respiration releases less energy than aerobic respiration
Respiration takes place mainly in the mitochondria
Water is produced during aerobic respiration

whyQuestions.q: Why do your muscles ache and tire during a hard sprint?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: oxygen runs low so muscles switch to anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid and less energy

whyQuestions.q: Why do we need to keep breathing in oxygen all the time?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: oxygen is needed continuously to break down glucose and keep releasing energy as ATP

whyQuestions.q: Why is respiration in a way the opposite of photosynthesis?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: respiration uses oxygen and glucose and releases carbon dioxide, reversing what photosynthesis builds

misconceptions: Respiration is the same thing as breathing
Respiration only happens in the lungs
Plants do not respire, they only photosynthesise
